name: Frame
summary: Presents one piece of content so it stands on its own (owner Q88, docs/spacing.md#framing-presenting-one-piece-of-content): its own room sized to the window and isolated from what's around it. To spacing it's one unit (Q94): its parent places it at the parent's gap, measured from its outer edge, and inside it the spacing method starts again (its content is a tree of its own). Never a box: space first, an optional edge-to-edge tone second, no border or shadow. It steps down with the window (Q89): a peek stage becomes a feature on a narrow window and its content's height on a short one; a feature drops to flow when its space would pass a third of the window's height. Not for lists, grids, forms or anything a person works through (they flow), and at most one stage per page. Frame only what gains from being read alone (Q91): a task or reference page (tickets, a schedule, a list, a detail page) never frames its heading away from the content people came for.
a11y: No role of its own; the content inside carries its semantics (a figure, a header, a section).

props.name: kind
props.description: `feature`: a band with its own fluid space above and below (a quote, a statement, a call to action). `stage`: a share of the window's height with the content centred in it (a page's opening, a status message).

props.name: mode
props.description: `peek` (default): framed, with part of the next (and, scrolled, the previous) content left in view to invite exploring; a stage leaves at least `c.frame.peek` of the next band showing. `distraction-free`: the content fills the window below the header, centred, with nothing else in view: for a piece that is the page's whole point (a status or error screen, a confirmation) (owner Q90).

props.name: ground
props.description: A quiet tone behind the band, edge to edge of the window: only when space alone can't separate it from busy neighbours.
